clue.text: Caught at rack initially taking favourite dress down

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letters of the words at and rack

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone caught with a dress off the rack, their favourite, being taken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'at rack', giving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be called in and reprimanded, the same as being dressed down.

clue.text: One speaking Mass, complete on the radio

parts.note: a cake is a mass of something, as in a cake of soap

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: whole means complete, entire

explanation.surface: A priest saying Mass, broadcast in full on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks religious, but means a lump, a cake. Only the word for complete is heard over the air. Cakehole is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cakehole is British slang for the mouth, the organ you talk with.

clue.text: Nasal problem: factor in blood disorder is in it

parts.note: Rh is the rhesus factor in blood

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of is in it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nose complaint caused by a factor found in a blood disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks medical but rearranges ISINIT into INITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinitis is inflammation of the lining of the nose, as with hay fever or colds.

clue.text: Moral approach seem in yonder people promoting energy

indicators.note: promoting means moving a letter up, to the front in a down clue

parts.note: those people over there, yonder
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A moral stance seen among distant folk who promote energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting energy' moves the E of THOSE to the top. 'seem in' is probably a slip for 'seen in', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding moral character and set of values of a person or group.

clue.text: Vulgar book about second public gathering

parts.note: flash means showy in a vulgar way
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A crude book about a second public meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash mob is a crowd that assembles suddenly in a public place by prior arrangement.

clue.text: Flaxen stuff, looking old, covering ends of settee

indicators.note: covering means the word for looking old wraps round the end letters

parts.note: a lined face is wrinkled and looks old

indicators.note: ends of picks the outside letters of settee

explanation.surface: A tired-looking flax-coloured throw covering the arms of a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking old' is a description of a lined, wrinkled face.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed is the seed of the flax plant, pressed for linseed oil.

clue.text: Science time in comprehensive — picked up a hint

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the reversed word
picked up means lifted, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: all-in means comprehensive, including everything

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school's science lesson raises just a trace of an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns ALLIN into NILLA, and 'in' puts T into it to give NTILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, so a hint of something.

clue.text: Primate ready to receive king

indicators.note: to receive means the cash word takes in the king letter

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash, money
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A primate poised to welcome a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like an adjective, but 'the ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkeys are members of the primate order, alongside apes and humans.

clue.text: Stage fellows carrying one end of banner …

indicators.note: carrying means the fellows word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: bods is informal British for people, fellows
a means one

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of banner

explanation.surface: Stagehands holding up one end of a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The boards is theatre slang for the stage, as in treading the boards.

clue.text: Black Prince, say, is reported as something black

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard spoken rather than read, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: night is a black thing, as in black as night

explanation.surface: The Black Prince is described as something dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Prince was Edward, eldest son of Edward III, one of the first members of the Order of the Garter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Prince was a knight of the Garter, so he is an example of the class.

clue.text: Official marks popular gain and is made to look daft

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: made to look daft says the letters of gain and is are messed about into a silly new order

explanation.surface: Official marks win popularity yet end up looking silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to look daft' rearranges GAIN and IS into SIGNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems showing official rank or membership.

clue.text: … left over from farewell performance?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken away from the farewell

parts.note: so long is an informal goodbye
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Following on from the banner clue: what remains after a farewell show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left over' looks like 'remaining' but gives L and O, taken from SO LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is a piece sung to an audience, an example of a performance.

clue.text: Ethanol is unexpectedly obtained in precipitate?

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters of ethanol is come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A chemistry experiment where ethanol yields an unexpected solid precipitate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges ETHANOLIS. The question mark flags the pun: a precipitate in chemistry, but here falling weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation is rain, snow or hail falling, so a single ball of ice is one bit of it.

clue.text: Source of Thames produced water for river

indicators.note: the source of a river is its start, so the first letter of Thames is taken

parts.note: wee'd means urinated, produced water

explanation.surface: At the Thames's source someone relieved themselves into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: WEE'D is a colloquial past tense of wee, to urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river forming part of the border between England and Scotland.

clue.text: The French, with one difficult problem: capturing zone in German city

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: capturing means the problem word holds the zone letter inside it

parts.note: a pig of a job is a hard, awkward one

explanation.surface: French visitors, and one tricky problem, take over a zone of a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leipzig is a major city in Saxony in eastern Germany.

clue.text: Is to go wild about lecturer supporting rising Australian scientist

indicators.note: supporting means coming below in a down clue, after the previous piece
rising means read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the lecturer letter
wild means the letters of is to go are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone told to go wild about a lecturer backing an up-and-coming Australian scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is to go' looks like a phrase of the surface but is the fodder for 'wild'. The result is wrapped round L ('about') and placed under ZO; 'rising' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoologist is a scientist who studies animals.

clue.text: Unexciting? Accordingly cut line

indicators.note: cut means the word for accordingly loses its tail letter

parts.note: duly means accordingly, as expected

explanation.surface: Something boring, so a line is accordingly cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull means boring and lacking interest, the opposite of exciting.

clue.text: Raised concerns about setter becoming divine?

indicators.note: about means the reversed worries wrap round the setter's name
raised means turned upwards in a down clue

parts.note: cares are worries, concerns
Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: Raising worries about a setter being promoted to the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' here is Phi himself, the puzzle's compiler; 'Raised' reads the worries upwards to give SERAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphic means like a seraph, an angel, so heavenly or divine.

clue.text: Star turn finishing early after bow before our group

indicators.note: after places the shortened turn behind the bow
before places the shortened turn ahead of our group

parts.note: an arc is a bow shape

indicators.note: finishing early means the last letter of turn is dropped

parts.note: us means our group

explanation.surface: A star act ends early after taking a bow ahead of the rest of the troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star turn' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Star' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcturus is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes.

clue.text: Supporting entry of Minister in ceremony

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: entry is the start, so the first letter of Minister is taken

explanation.surface: Backing the arrival of a minister at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Form means set procedure or ritual, as in a matter of form.

clue.text: Old woman covering a blemish in cosmetic

indicators.note: covering means the woman word goes round the other letters

parts.note: ma is mother, an old woman in slang
a scar is a mark, a blemish

explanation.surface: An elderly woman uses make-up to hide a skin mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up applied to darken eyelashes, a cosmetic.

clue.text: A lot of the ambience around colleague comes from ham

indicators.note: around means the shortened word wraps itself about the colleague
a lot of means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: an aura is the distinctive atmosphere or ambience of a place
a mate is a workmate, a colleague

explanation.surface: A lot of atmosphere around a colleague comes from a hammy performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims the final letter, leaving AUR. 'ham' looks like a bad actor but means a radio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham radio operator is an amateur enthusiast; ham also means an unskilled performer.

clue.text: Sally of timeless mockery?

indicators.note: timeless means the time letter is dropped

parts.note: a taunt is an act of mockery

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally subjected to endless ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a fairground figure thrown at, so a target of ridicule; 'Sally' points to her title.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally is the old fairground target, so Sally's title supplies the word.

clue.text: Equipment orbiting Earth or Venus?

indicators.note: orbiting means going around, so the equipment surrounds the earth letter

parts.note: plant is industrial machinery, equipment

explanation.surface: Kit circling the Earth, or perhaps Venus.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is an example of a world circling the Sun, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Collided with small vehicle

parts.note: a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Crashed into a small vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck means hit, and to have hit something is to have collided with it.

clue.text: Drunk unable to open house

indicators.note: unable to open means the word for drunk loses its first letter

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk who can't get the door of his house open.
explanation.walkthrough: House (or housey-housey) is an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance played with numbered cards, the same game as bingo or house.

clue.text: Components of antimony finally used to engrave?

parts.note: antimony's chemical symbol is Sb, made of the letters S and B
used finally means used last

explanation.surface: Parts of the metal antimony are used at the end for engraving.
explanation.walkthrough: Sb, the symbol for antimony, has two components: S and B, written out with the word and between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandblasting can etch designs into glass or stone, a form of engraving, hence the question mark.

clue.text: British taking stand in French port

parts.note: a rest is a stand or support

explanation.surface: A Briton takes a stand in a French harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a naval port in Brittany, north-west France.

clue.text: A lunatic at sea on a ship?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of a lunatic are jumbled

explanation.surface: A madman out on the ocean aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ALUNATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to sailors and ships, so anything on board a vessel qualifies.

clue.text: Woman's behind curtain material in the lower area

indicators.note: behind places the woman's word after the curtain material

parts.note: net is fine mesh fabric used for curtains
her is a woman's pronoun; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A woman hides behind the net curtain downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or situated underneath, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Pop group try this punch?

definitions.meaning: a British boy band of the 1990s led by Gary Barlow
the cry of someone landing a blow

explanation.surface: A band invited to sample a fruit punch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tasting a drink; the second sense is the shout as a fist lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The British boy band and the triumphant cry share the words; both readings are idioms.

clue.text: Keeps a device for punishment

definitions.meaning: a shop that keeps an item has it for sale
a wooden frame holding the ankles of offenders for public humiliation

explanation.surface: A castle's keeps held a device for punishing prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop carrying goods is said to have them in; the old pillory-like frame shares the word.
